question: Is the label noise in LLM-generated, manually screened time-sensitive legal QA sets low enough to detect a hard-versus-graded temporal ranking difference, and does the planned experiment need a label-audit arm?
description: The closest benchmark accepted 312 of 697 generated QA pairs, using LLM generation plus manual screening. If a substantial share of retained items are mislabeled or do not truly require the intended version, the label noise floor may exceed the effect size of a hard-versus-graded ranking change, making any crossover finding undetectable. Expert validation reduces but does not eliminate this.
rationale: A null result from the crossover experiment would be uninterpretable if label noise prevents detecting the effect at all, so the noise floor must be estimated before concluding anything.
